quote.text: A properly educated leader, especially when harassed and under pressure, will know from his study of history and the classics that circumstances very much like those he is encountering have occurred from time to time on this earth since the beginning of history. He will avoid the self-indulgent error of seeing himself in a predicament so unprecedented, so unique, as to justify his making an exception to law, custom or morality in favor of himself. The making of such exceptions has been the theme of public life throughout much of our lifetimes. For twenty years, we've been surrounded by gamesmen unable to cope with the wisdom of the ages. They make exceptions to law and custom in favor of themselves because they choose to view ordinary dilemmas as unprecedented crises.
quote.author: James B. Stockdale
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Just as history reminds us that challenges recur, understand that parenting, too, is a journey repeating timeless lessons; rely on well-established virtues rather than making personal exceptions when guiding your children.
    • Instill in your family the importance of adhering to moral and ethical standards, ensuring that each decision and lesson remains rooted in the wisdom of ages rather than in momentary crisis or personal bias.
  • Leadership
    • In the role of a leader, remember that many of the dilemmas you face are not unprecedented; the annals of history and the classics provide ample examples of resilience, reinforcing that consistency and principled conduct are paramount.
    • Avoid succumbing to the temptation of self-serving shortcuts; instead, let the examples of past leaders bolster your resolve to uphold law, custom, and morality, ensuring that your decisions benefit the collective rather than just yourself.
  • Product Management
    • Much like historical challenges, product management often confronts recurring dilemmas; appreciate that crisis is rarely unique, and rely on proven methods and established practices to guide innovation and problem-solving.
    • Maintain discipline and consistency in process and strategy, resisting the lure to bypass standards for temporary gains, and instead, anchor your approach in the time-tested principles that have consistently driven successful projects.
